nodes.label: arboard's Wayland Clipboard is a zero-sized struct, so every method opens its own connection
nodes.norm_label: arboard wayland clipboard is a zero sized struct
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r8-clipboard-consumer-regression-audit [ses_f1cfc8e35ffeKbB3t3sXRX5bTm].md:L4248] arboard's X11 `Clipboard` is a **global singleton** (`x11.rs:910` `inner: Arc<Inner>`, one `serve_requests` thread, `x11.rs:915-919` returns a cached `Arc`). arboard's Wayland `Clipboard` is a **zero-sized struct** (`wayland.rs:28`) and *every method* opens its own connection and roundtrips.

nodes.label: wl-clipboard-rs copy in non-foreground mode serves the selection from a detached thread
nodes.norm_label: wl clipboard rs copy serves from a detached thread
nodes.rationale:
Two anchors because the reason wraps: it is not just that set_text returns, but that the offering is then owned by a thread whose death empties the clipboard. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r8-clipboard-consumer-regression-audit [ses_f1cfc8e35ffeKbB3t3sXRX5bTm].md:L3770] wl-clipboard-rs spawns a separate thread to serve the copy requests and `copy()` returns.
[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r8-clipboard-consumer-regression-audit [ses_f1cfc8e35ffeKbB3t3sXRX5bTm].md:L3772] If that source is dropped/destroyed, the clipboard becomes empty.

nodes.label: The clipboard polling monitor opens three fresh Wayland connections every 500 ms
nodes.norm_label: polling monitor opens three wayland connections per tick
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r8-clipboard-consumer-regression-audit [ses_f1cfc8e35ffeKbB3t3sXRX5bTm].md:L3776] So **3 fresh Wayland connections every 500 ms = 6 connections/sec, ~8640 connections/minute, forever while the app runs.** That is the most concrete new cost.

nodes.label: The #{selection} restore clobbers the selection the app just copied

nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r8-clipboard-consumer-regression-audit [ses_f1cfc8e35ffeKbB3t3sXRX5bTm].md:L3806] If the user hits `#{selection}`, the selection they copied is gone from their clipboard and replaced by the pre-selection content. Under X11 the user's native clipboard was untouched.

nodes.label: Clipboard writes go through the external wl-copy process while reads go through in-process data-control
nodes.norm_label: wl copy writer and data control reader are two mechanisms
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r8-clipboard-consumer-regression-audit [ses_f1cfc8e35ffeKbB3t3sXRX5bTm].md:L4283] Injection writes via the external `wl-copy` process (`cmd_builder.rs`), backups/restores/silent copies via an in-process arboard serve thread, and reads via data-control. All three are the same clipboard, but three different ownership mechanisms with different lifetimes; the restore in item 3 races the `wl-copy` child.
